spec.name: Quiet names v32
spec.notes: Long the calm names, short the jumpy ones.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 2.0, annual return 7%, maximum drawdown 5%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.99 to 2.09 (change +0.09).
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 1.99 to -0.08. Changed by strict mode: operators zscore_full, winsor_full.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 1.93 (as submitted, 5 bps: 1.99); it breaks even at 157.0 bps with daily turnover 0.02.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 1.99 against 1.99 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period (strict mode, 10 bps) the Sharpe ratio is 0.54 against 1.99 in research, a gap of +1.45.
The best year gives 17% of total P&L (year 5) and calm regimes give 56%; Sharpe is 1.69 in calm and 2.96 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 2 distinct specs; the best of 2 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.00, so the claimed 2.00 becomes 2.00 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 2.03 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean -0.04, 95th percentile 0.52).
Perturbing the 2 numeric values in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.99 to as low as 1.09 (as low as 1.66 at 25%).
The top 1% of days (20 days) give 32% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 17% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first
